description:
Fixture 01253 (1,000 sequential calls): heap+pop compiles 26.1 s to 84 MB; d7w (ddf2c18e6) 4.3 s / 3.1 MB. Copying every live value per continuation is quadratic. First run the experiment: (a) copy-on-old: a write into a frame first checks it is young, else copies it to the tip; (b) linked write-once frames: each step builds a frame of only its new values plus a parent pointer. Measure both on 01253 (compile, binary, run) and the distiller. Prediction: both within 2x of d7w's compile time and size, distiller unchanged within noise. Fallback if both miss: d7w as built plus a remembered set. Build the winner.
Then: PR #543 closes unmerged; fz-d7w's description is updated to point here.
Acceptance: 01253 compiles within 2x of 4.3 s and 3.1 MB on run and build; no assert_written_object_is_young trips.
Proposal (approved 2026-11-14): https://claude.ai/artifact/94aN2YPxunzwVEzct26nz2 (local /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-d7w.html). Spike evidence: worktree ../fz-hc, branch exp/heap-cont-reads (uncommitted, FZ_SPIKE_* switches).

comments.text: DECIDED 2026-11-14 by experiment (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/d1d265b3-f8e7-419b-8316-906f89c17e6b/scratchpad/9x7-3: 9x7-3-spike-all-candidates.patch, predictions.md, sweep-results.txt, ret-results.txt, matrix.log). Design: copy-on-old body frames. A chain of >=16 continuations each built by exactly one other shares one heap frame (d7w's construction-site and held-slot analysis); every frame store first checks the frame lies in [block_start, bump_top) and otherwise copies it to the tip (fz_frame_copy_to_tip) and writes there, so no write lands in an object a collection kept. Dead boxed slots are cleared (skipping scalar-kinded slots: a scalar ref names its own slot). Measured: 01253 build 51.4 s/51.2 MB -> ~3 s/3.27 MB, run and build print 501500; distiller and 1M map unchanged (frame-resident entries 133 of 74M); copy ran 1/77/60 times. Rejected by data: linked write-once frames (quadratic chain walk; skip pointers 2.09x size, +25% RSS), a words-based structural rule (keeps short chains that lose their pop: map 301 MB), the last-member release (no-op at T=16). Threshold sweep 0..64: knee at 4 (map) / 8 (distiller), flat 16..64. Clear: dead 10M list held by a frame -> peak 2588 -> 1872 MB, copied 1693 -> 1438 MB; live control and distiller unchanged. Pins: map_atom_order 250/11184 -> 245/11024 (five closures share one frame); a_large_list_passed_back_and_forth yield 32160 -> 32176 (a member that needs no values of its own still carries the shared frame's width: 32 -> 48 B). Poison 2/2, matrix 3440 passed + those 3. Base run of 01253 panics in cranelift-jit PosOverflow at 51 MB of code (fixed by this ticket's size drop).

title: A long body keeps one frame without writing into a kept object
